Quibus si inter se convenire nequit, secedentes deliberant, & suffragijs inter se certant; nonnunquam etiam tripartito dividunt sese, vt supra ostendi, cum de agro agerem seorsim: atq; ita, si duæ partes in unam sententiam eant, tertia quoq; trahunt. Tum, quod sentiunt, per Syndicum quoq; suum, quem habent, senatui exponunt. Post disputationes vbi consensere senatus agrarijq;, decretum conficitur, atq; in publicum librum refertur. Decretum totam obligat provinciam.
main_text.head: DE RE ECCLESIASTICA IN URBE.
main_text.p: Res eccle-siastica in urbe.Sic civilia: restat, vt ecclesiastica perstrin-gam. Solent in urbe esse, vt in principio ostendi, parochiæ tres cum totidem fanis. In his sacerdotes sacris operantes numero XXI: in quibus pastores tres singulì singulis in fanis ac parochijs. Tandem anno M. CCCC. LXXX unus ex his editus velut ἐφορος totius rei ecclesiasticæ in urbe & urbis vicinia, quem PERSONAM more suo vocabant: isq; erat velut minor quidam episcopus, aut episcopi vicem gerens, magna potestate & multis privilegijs ornatus à Romano Pontifice. Hunc cæteri pastores, & duo seniores urbis consules eligebant, & in munus suum

page.notes: The chapter heading is set in large spaced capitals and is given as a level 1 title without a caput number, since no number is printed. The Greek word after "velut" is uncertain: it is transcribed as ἐφορος, and the trailing mark may be a printing flourish, not a letter. The word "consensere" is read with some doubt. Several long s characters are read as plain s; the word "fanis" in the first paragraph could also be read as "sanis". The left margin note is an ordinary marginal note placed beside the first paragraph. The bottom line "suum" is the last printed line on this page; the text continues on the next page.
